description:
Approved scope: PRD Phase 1 Connect foundation plus backend functions needed by later Person self-service. User approved implementation of all remaining slices; current task implements only .3. Include schema migrations for Connect (NOT AI credential migration), generic resolver, authenticated Person grant operations, OAuth start/callback/reconnect/refresh, safe mutation events, Person merge/deletion, security and tests. Exclude AIProviderCredential association/backfill, Factory/ProviderSpec/ServerManager changes, actual Agent invalidation, BO screens, Person screens/session implementation, Data Source/MCP adoption, and workflow Actor propagation. These remain separate slices.

Infrastructure audit: actual namespace is Zaq.Engine.Connect. credential.ex owns reusable provider configuration; grant.ex owns context-bound grants. Existing grants require resource_type/resource_id, owners org/user, auth kinds api_key/oauth2/jwt_bearer, and have no ownership uniqueness. Existing Credential also stores API-key/JWT secrets. OAuth and refresh already exist; Engine API exposes internal Connect operations. ActorNormalizer normalizes rather than authenticates. People.delete_person and PersonMerger currently omit Connect grants. Existing routing is not a durable transactional outbox; Oban is available.

Architecture decisions: add a credential-bound grant lane without rewriting legacy resource-bound consumers; no provider-wide matching; no new resolver fallback to secrets on Credential. Keep user ownership and user_level unchanged. One current credential-bound grant row per credential and owner across all statuses; revoke retains the row and blocks optional fallback, explicit removal permits absence/fallback. Historical events retain IDs, not secrets. SUPERSEDING USER-APPROVED REVISION: no binding_type or dedicated person_id column. Reuse owner_type/owner_id with person and resource_type/resource_id with connect_credential. Derive canonical resource coordinates server-side and enforce resource_id = credential_id::text with a NULL-safe DB CHECK plus the existing credential_id FK. Person referential integrity is checked at the trusted application storage boundary; concurrent orphan risk is accepted. No triggers, guard rows or extra Person FK. Use partial unique indexes for person and org canonical rows, handling NULL org owner IDs explicitly. Changes remain opt-in; existing resource-bound selection and AI runtime are untouched.

Security: trusted execution actor may reach internal resolver; Person management must require authenticated Person context from a trusted adapter, never an arbitrary request map. Nil actor selects global only in privileged runtime resolution; nil never authorizes management or reveals secrets. Public/event management replies use allowlisted DTOs. ResolvedCredential is internal runtime-only, redacted, and never emitted via generic read actions. Credential-owned OAuth client settings never become Person-editable. API key/private key/token inputs are write-only and strictly encrypted. No raw provider error bodies, authorization codes, token payloads, or unrestricted metadata in responses/events/telemetry.

Compatibility: preserve current consumers while introducing explicit canonical management APIs. Policy/global-grant completeness validation applies at the new atomic configuration boundary, not retrospectively to every legacy credential changeset. JWT credential-required secret validation must support canonical grant-owned JWT material without weakening existing legacy mode. No migration copies company credentials to People. Later AI migration must populate canonical grants before switching reads.

Delivery: test-first issues, one focused PR per issue where practical, no implementation until planning dependencies are validated. OAuth and refresh are split because of independent security/concurrency surfaces; identity cleanup is a separate Accounts-owned integration. Keep a serial dependency chain to provide safe delivery gates; it is intentionally stricter than theoretical parallelism, without diamonds. Documentation and tests accompany every step. Require >=95% touched-file coverage or explicit measured exception and follow-up, mix format after code edits, focused tests and final mix q.

Follow-on contracts: mutation delivery provides secret-free credential/person/grant dependencies and UUID event identity (no artificial monotonic revision) for later distributed Agent consumers. This slice does not claim to invalidate Agents or provide end-to-end BYOK. Future Agent subscriber must ensure all owning nodes receive events and close server-creation-versus-invalidation races; single NodeRouter invocation is not evidence of broadcast. Workflow scope actor work is not a prerequisite to testing Connect directly. Coordinate identity compatibility with zaq-r35/zaq-u3g and coverage debt zaq-c1k.

Open delivery gate: before enabling public self-service endpoints, identify and verify the trusted Person session adapter; if none exists, ship tested backend functions only and document that transport adapter as deferred. Do not invent a Person login system in this slice. Architecture approval is the user Go following the seven-step foundation outline; implementation refinements that materially change product/security semantics require renewed approval.

2026-09-14 FINAL USER-APPROVED STORAGE DECISION: canonical grants reuse owner_type/owner_id (org with NULL ID or person with non-null ID) and resource_type=connect_credential/resource_id=credential_id string. Native type/shape and explicit non-null/equality CHECKs plus existing credential_id FK; partial unique org/person slots across statuses. No binding_type, duplicate person_id, extra Person FK, triggers or guard rows. Server derives resource pair and configuration auth fields; secret_binding stays independent. Trusted canonical storage checks literal current active Person, without authenticating callers or resolving aliases. Concurrent orphan grants/secrets are an accepted residual risk. IDs must not be reused operationally; no silent reidentification through stale aliases; synchronous erasure is not guaranteed. Later resolver must check Person exists/eligible BEFORE policy selection even disabled, and missing/stale Person errors NEVER fall back globally. Authenticated writes and OAuth/refresh must recheck current identity; lifecycle cleanup/reconciliation and later distributed server invalidation remain unimplemented in storage task .1.

2026-09-14 approved delivery order: graph LR; S1 --> S2; S2 --> S3; S3 --> S5; S5 --> S6; S6 --> S7; S7 --> S4; S4 --> S8; S8 --> S9. Both dependency directions verified against full acyclic DAG; external edges preserved. .1/.2 remain in_progress pending merge; clean workspace at d0c0df9b contains prior implementation. Implement only .3 now, no commit/push/new worktree. .3 uses transactional Oban jobs and synchronous Agent.Events/NodeRouter dispatch; dedicated connect_credential_notifications queue deliberately unconsumed in all dev/production role configurations until actual Agent receiver and owning-node fanout ship later. Always enqueue; no stub receiver, direct PubSub, ServerManager call, monotonic revision or consumer acknowledgment guarantee.

comments.text: Plan expanded into nine independently reviewable steps: approved step 2 split into canonical mutations and durable events; approved step 5 split into OAuth authorization and refresh. Serial delivery is intentional to avoid exposing unsafe partial personal flows. Mermaid sequence: graph LR; S1[Storage] --> S2[Mutations]; S2 --> S3[Events]; S3 --> S4[Resolver]; S4 --> S5[Person API]; S5 --> S6[OAuth]; S6 --> S7[Refresh]; S7 --> S8[Person lifecycle]; S8 --> S9[Validation]. Planning only: application files unchanged; implementation tasks remain open. Existing Beadwork searches for person grant, credential policy and Connect foundation found no matching active plan.

Dependency validation completed: exact blocked_by/blocks edges verified for all nine issues, all five required planning sections present, serial DAG acyclic with no diamonds. Open epics hide children in bw ready; epic activated for plan tracking, then bw ready confirmed zaq-jrg.1 as sole ready child. All implementation children remain open and no application changes have started.

Planning closeout: mix q completed with exit 0 (docs generation and Credo: 1177 source files, no issues). git status --short clean afterward. No application code changed, no commits or PR created. This check is baseline validation, not evidence that planned feature tests exist or pass.

.3 completed-uncommitted and validated; remains in_progress pending review/merge, as do prior .1/.2. Final exact serial dependency graph verified both directions and full graph acyclic: .1 -> .2 -> .3 -> .5 -> .6 -> .7 -> .4 -> .8 -> .9; external dependencies preserved. Only .3 implemented in this task. Detailed APIs/coverage/exact commands/limits in .3 comments. Parent proceeds with .5 under user-approved sequence; queue activation remains deferred to actual Agent receiver/fanout.
